definition: Learning skills are the abilities used to learn, which can vary in strength and may be affected by mild to moderate deficits. In this source, they are described as being related to executive functioning and to academic attainment.

reasons: The packet does not define “learning skills” as “the abilities used to learn,” nor does it explicitly state that they “can vary in strength.”

The packet supports that the study examines impairments in executive functions and learning skills, and evaluates relationships between executive functions, learning skills, and academic attainment; however, it does not explicitly state that learning skills are “related to executive functioning” and “to academic attainment” in the definitional sense used.

The packet supports the idea that “mild to moderate deficits have a significant impact on learning skills” (as a hypothesis), but the remainder of the definition includes claims not directly supported by the provided text.
The packet does not define learning skills as “the abilities used to learn”; it only reports a study about impairments in executive functions and learning skills.

“May be affected by mild to moderate deficits” is not supported as a general definition; the packet says the authors hypothesized that mild to moderate deficits in executive functioning have a significant impact on learning skills.
The link to executive functioning and academic attainment is only presented as a study aim to evaluate relationships, not as a settled definitional statement.
